newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Latin coffee producers say stocks under control.
newsitem.headline: Latin coffee producers say stocks under control.

text.p: Seven Latin American coffee producers said export quotas succeeded in keeping down their customers' coffee stocks.

"The group of delegates of participating countries revised the progress of the agreements...arriving at the conclusion that the proposed objective of not accumulating excessive coffee stocks in consumer countries has been achieved," said a communique issued by the CEV group of producers at the end of a meeting in Quito late Monday.
Representives of CEV countries Venezuela, Ecuador, Honduras, Nicaragua, Costa Rica and El Salvador attended the meeting, as well as delegates from Colombia and Brazil.

The communique also called for continued dialogue with Guatemala and Mexico to reach an agreement with the Association of Coffee Producing Countries for "cooperation that supports the price of the bean in the international markets." It called on the Ecuadoran government to contact the Mexicans and Guatemalans on the group's behalf.

Participants at the meeting analyzed measures taken to meet export quotas agreed for 1996/97. The communique highlighted moves by Brazil to support its coffee producers, including the planned creation of a Coffee Council to fix state policies for coffee production, sales and exports.
Delegates had said they would use the Quito meeting to prepare common positions for upcoming meetings of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries and of the International Coffee Organization.
